metaData.title: OpenAI Model Disproves   80-Year-Old Math Conjecture
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: An OpenAI model has autonomously disproved a nearly 80-year-old conjecture in combinatorial geometry, the Erdős unit distance problem, by constructing point configurations with a polynomial improvement over the previously best-known square grid construction.
metaData.summary: This article announces a significant breakthrough in mathematics achieved by an internal OpenAI reasoning model. The model has solved the Erdős unit distance problem, a longstanding open problem in combinatorial geometry that asks for the maximum number of unit-distance pairs among n points in the plane. For decades, the prevailing belief was that the 'square grid' construction was essentially optimal. The AI model disproved this conjecture by providing an infinite family of examples that yield a polynomial improvement, achieving at least n^(1+δ) unit-distance pairs for a fixed δ > 0. The proof, which has been verified by external mathematicians, ingeniously applies sophisticated tools from algebraic number theory, such as infinite class field towers, to an elementary geometric question. This marks the first time an AI has autonomously resolved a prominent open problem central to a subfield of mathematics. The article highlights the implications for AI as a research partner, demonstrating its ability to hold together complex arguments, connect distant ideas, and produce work that survives expert scrutiny, with potential applications beyond mathematics in fields like physics and biology.

mainPoints.point: An OpenAI model has autonomously solved the Erdős unit distance problem, a nearly 80-year-old open problem in combinatorial geometry.
mainPoints.explanation: The model disproved the long-held conjecture that the square grid construction was optimal, providing a new construction that achieves a polynomial improvement in the number of unit-distance pairs.

mainPoints.point: The proof ingeniously applies deep concepts from algebraic number theory to an elementary geometric question.
mainPoints.explanation: The solution uses tools like infinite class field towers and Golod-Shafarevich theory, creating an unexpected bridge between number theory and discrete geometry.

mainPoints.point: This is the first time an AI has autonomously resolved a prominent open problem central to a subfield of mathematics.
mainPoints.explanation: The result marks a milestone for AI in mathematics, demonstrating the system's capacity for deep reasoning, original ideas, and producing work that passes expert scrutiny.

mainPoints.point: The result signifies a new kind of collaboration between AI and human mathematicians.
mainPoints.explanation: The AI's solution was enriched by a companion paper from external mathematicians, who provided deeper context and a refined understanding of the discovery.

keyQuotes: This proof is an important milestone for the math and AI communities. It marks the first time that a prominent open problem, central to a subfield of mathematics, has been solved autonomously by AI.

According to leading number theorist Arul Shankar, 'In my opinion this paper demonstrates that current AI models go beyond just helpers to human mathematicians -- they are capable of having original ingenious ideas, and then carrying them out to fruition'.
The unexpected connection between algebraic number theory and discrete geometry revealed by the solution is part of what makes the result notable.
AI is helping us to more fully explore the cathedral of mathematics we have build over the centuries; what other unseen wonders are waiting in the wings?
AI can help search, suggest, and verify. People choose the problems that matter, interpret the results, and decide what questions to pursue next.

relatedArticles.title: Sam Altman + Greg Brockman - On The Great OpenAI Reset
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Sam Altman and Greg Brockman discuss OpenAI's journey, the shift towards personal AGI and agent infrastructure, the jagged frontier of AI capabilities, and the societal implications of abundant compute and intelligence.

relatedArticles.title: Codex for (almost) everything
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces a major update to Codex, expanding its capabilities beyond coding to include computer operation, web interaction, image generation, and deeper integration across the software development lifecycle with new features like memory, automations, and over 90 plugins.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.4 with Native Computer Use and 1M Context
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Sam Altman announces the release of GPT-5.4, featuring enhanced knowledge work, native computer use, and a 1-million-token context window.

relatedArticles.title: Advancing voice intelligence with new models in the API
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces three new audio models in the API—GPT-Realtime-2, GPT-Realtime-Translate, and GPT-Realtime-Whisper—to enable more intelligent, natural, and actionable real-time voice applications for developers.

relatedArticles.title: This is ChatGPT Images 2.0
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI has officially launched Images 2.0, a highly intelligent image generation model capable of 'thinking', web searching, generating complex diagrams, supporting multilingual prompts, and creating coherent multi-image sets for professional production.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing GPT-5.5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI releases GPT-5.5, its most capable model yet, with significant gains in agentic coding, knowledge work, and scientific research, while maintaining GPT-5.4 latency and improving token efficiency.

relatedArticles.title: Codex Now Integrates Directly with Chrome on macOS and Windows
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces a new Chrome extension for Codex on macOS and Windows, enabling the AI to operate directly within a user's live browser session to perform complex, parallel automation tasks using their active profile and direct code execution.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing workspace agents in ChatGPT
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces workspace agents, a new class of shared, long-running AI agents within ChatGPT for business teams, designed to automate complex workflows, integrate with organizational tools, and operate under enterprise-grade controls.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Introduces GPT-5.5: A New Class of Intelligence for Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces GPT-5.5, a new model designed for complex goal understanding and autonomous task completion, now available in ChatGPT and Codex.

relatedArticles.title: Building a safe， effective sandbox to enable Codex on Windows
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the engineering journey of building a custom sandbox for Codex on Windows, from an initial unelevated prototype using SIDs and write-restricted tokens to a final elevated design that leverages dedicated Windows users and firewall rules for robust network isolation.
